newsitem.title: USA: Conrail, CSX work on new pact, key issues remain.
newsitem.headline: Conrail, CSX work on new pact, key issues remain.

text.p: Conrail Inc. and CSX Corp. spent Tuesday hammering out details of a $10.3 billion transaction to end a four-month takeover battle and re-route the East Coast's railroad network.

Sources close to the situation said key details still had not been finalised, including whether Conrail would be sold to CSX or whether CSX and rival Norfolk Southern Corp. would make a joint bid for the Philadelphia-based railroad.
However, the sources were confident that a final deal will likely be struck soon in which Richmond, Va.-based CSX and Norfolk, Va.-based Norfolk Southern will share Conrail's routes.
"You're talking now about a very technically complex situation. Nothing is signed and nothing is decided until something is signed," said one source, who declined to be identified.
Conrail broke a five-week silence on Monday to confirm it was negotiating a revision to its $9.6 billion merger agreement with CSX for a deal that would be valued at $10.3 billion, or $115 per share.

Conrail was pressured to negotiate a new deal with CSX in order to match a competing bid from Norfolk Southern and break a stalemate in the takeover fight. Conrail shareholders in January had rejected a key measure in the Conrail-CSX pact that was crucial for the transaction to proceed.
Conrail and CSX had no comment Tuesday on the negotiations.
Norfolk Southern, which late Monday applauded the move to end the stalemate, did not appear to be involved in Tuesday's discussions.
Although Conrail's board on Monday authorised the company to negotiate a deal at $115 per share, it was not immediately clear whether CSX directors had authorised the railroad to raise its bid.

Based on Tuesday's stock prices, the existing Conrail-CSX pact, which is a mixture of cash and stock, valued Conrail at about $109 per share. CSX previously has vowed that it would not raise its offer for Conrail.
In any case, sources said both boards would likely hold at least one meeting before a deal would be finalised.
In addition to determining the actual structure of a transaction, other key issues include the timing for shareholder payment and severance packages for top Conrail officials.

Wall Street remained optimistic about the likelihood of a transaction, while industry analysts assessed its impact on CSX and Norfolk Southern, especially in the area of cost savings to each railraod.
Shares of Conrail rose $1.25 to $112.875 on the New York Stock Exchange. CSX stock gained $1.25 to $50.25 and Norfolk Southern shares fell 87.5 cents to $93, also on NYSE.
